title: 2024 AMC 10B Problem 10
statement: Quadrilateral \(ABCD\) is a parallelogram, and \(E\) is the midpoint of the side \(\overline{AD}.\) Let \(F\) be the intersection of lines \(EB\) and \(AC.\) What is the ratio of the area of quadrilateral \(CDEF\) to the area of triangle \(CFB?\)

solutions.text: Area ratios don’t change under an affine map, so drop in convenient coordinates: \(A = (0,0),\) \(B = (1,0),\) \(C = (1,1),\) \(D = (0,1),\) which makes \(E = (0, \tfrac12).\) Line \(AC\) is \(y = x,\) and line \(EB\) runs from \((0, \tfrac12)\) to \((1, 0);\) they cross at \(F = (\tfrac13, \tfrac13).\) The shoelace formula gives quadrilateral \(CDEF\) area \(\tfrac{5}{12}\) and triangle \(CFB\) area \(\tfrac13.\) So the ratio is \(\tfrac{5}{12} : \tfrac13 = 5 : 4.\) Therefore, the answer is A.
hints: Area ratios are unchanged by an affine map, so compute with \(A = (0,0),\) \(B = (1,0),\) \(C = (1,1),\) \(D = (0,1)\)
Find \(F\) as the intersection of line \(AC\) with line \(EB,\) then use the shoelace formula
